title: Misbehaving by fellow BMTC Passengers
description:
It is often seen in BMTC customers keeping theri belongings on seat when bus arrives and then claiming to sit on the seat irrespective of coming late to the bus. Also, there is no action by conductors or drivers against such behaviour.

BMTC being public transport seats are available to customers on first come first serve basis except for physically challenged or senior citizens.

In a same incident today, a lady kept bag on seat when i was just about to sit (Please not i was not even far from the seat) and then started arguing with me to vacate the seat since she kept her bag their and has been travelling on that route since 25 years and the bus belongs to her father(Yes she said this). It was not only argument but she also physically started fighting with me. 

And the conductor and driver instead of asking her to get down or imposing fine on her asked me only to move. I have no problem in shifting to different seat and I understand it was not driver or conductor who started the fight, but this is general rule that there are no reservations in BMTC unlike KSRTC and conductor and driver being representative of BMTC services are responsible to maintain order.

Many times it is noticed that conductor and driver dont come forward to see who is actually wrong even in cases when a senior citizen is standing and while a young person is sitting in seats reserved for them.

The bus was for route "Singapura - Vidhana Soudha" 271c at 8:30 am on 24.1.19. Attached are images of scratch marks given by the lady to me also she even slapped me and pulled my hair and even then conductor did not take action against her.

title: Huge traffic jams due to AET Junction bottleneck
description:
From past 6 months, traffic has worsened on Sarjapura road near Doddakannelli stretch during peak office hours due to bottleneck at AET Junction. Unfortunately, there is no alternative roads towards Marathahalli  apart from just outer ring road and Doddakannelli-Kadubesnahalli Road. Hence, all the traffic on Sarjapura road is distributed on both the streches and causing huge pile up of traffic on this road. The road is unscientific as it is does not have uniform consistent width. To add to woes, there is no lane discipline and which makes narrow width stretches as bottle necks before the junction.

Most of the times these days, it takes about 45 mins to 1 hour to just cross the AET junction from Andhra Bank, Doddakannelli (~2 KMs of stretch). Due to this , there is a huge loss in fuel and precious time.

As a short term solution, I believe BBMP and Bangalore traffic police should think of alternatives to de congest the AET junction and should think of laying parallel roads to outer ring road as a long term solution. However, it is upto agencies to think of best solution for benefit of citizens and city.

I wanted to know if there is any action plan in place by BBMP, Government of Karnataka and Bangalore City Police to provide a near term and long term solution.

title: Miserable condition of Panathur-Belagere Road Railway Underpass
description:
Panathur, due to its proximity to Whitefield and Sarjapura, has seen rapid growth in the last 2 years and is now filled with commercial properties and apartment complexes. Sobha Dream Acres, a massive undertaking on the Panathur-Belagere Road, has 6500 flats. Prestige Lake View, another apartment complex, has around 4000 flats to its name. All told there should be more than 15000 flats. 
Being extremely narrow, this road can barely handle two-way traffic. It is filled with garbage and potholes and is perpetually being dug up on some pretext. The icing on the cake is a narrow railway vent at the end of this stretch which allows only one-way traffic to commute at a time. 
The menace on the Panathur-Belagere Road begins even before sunrise at times and continues for the rest of the day. Over 20,000 vehicles pass through this road daily where only one side is let to travel at a time. The presence of a large number of water tankers only adds to the chaos as these tanker drivers rush along with a complete disregard for traffic or rules. 
Making matters worse, the traffic on the Panathur-Belagere Road is not being managed by the city’s traffic police. This Herculean task falls to private security guards deployed by some IT companies.  Many people don’t conform to the guard’s instructions as they have no legal power to penalize anyone. 
The residents of Panathur have been waiting for years, in suspended animation, hoping to see a ray of light in what seems to be a never-ending tunnel of darkness.
location: Panathuru Cirlce, Kadubeesanahalli, Panathur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560103, India

title: Outer ring road is swept but the mud/sand etc is not picked up, instead left in mounds, along the roads, medians , on footpaths etc
description:
2 months back, i took a ride from Bellandur to Kalyan Nagar and back( I live in Bangalore ) with the specific intention of taking pictures along the outer ring road to capture the negligence of the authorities who are in charge of cleaning the roads in this stretch. In short here is what you see:
1) Mounds of sand/mud along the sides or medians of the ORR in many stretches including flyovers, maximum after the More flyover when going towards KR Puram station. These mounds are not natural formations, they have been made by someone, quite obvious by the people who have swept the road, perhaps with the intention that it would be picked up by another team , but then that has not happened. These mounds of mud still exist in after a month!
2) You can see the same mounds of mud and sand on the top portion of flyover to Kasturinagar from Tin Factory. The mud and sand are neatly arranged as small mountains( kids might love to see them !! ) on the footpath. Again they exist till date!!
3) The state of underpasses at the center of the underpass right under the bridge on top, should be seen, mainly the Ram Murthy Nagar and Horamavu underpass. You can see lot of sand/mud on the side of the road along with lot of the same accumulated on the footpaths. If a two wheeler goes towards the side of the roads in speed, the rider is sure of getting the "last ride".
I can go on and on listing such stuff. The same scenes can be seen on Indiranagar 100 ft road, sarjapur road, old airport road etc. I fail to understand this!! When someone has swept the road, am sure some money would have paid for doing the same, why is the stuff not being picked up!! Instead it is left lying there, in fact you can see plants growing in many of these sand/mud mounds!!
Can't Bangalore have cleaner roads, is it that difficult? Many a times citizens add to the mess by throwing garbage on top of these mounds of sand/mud. Please stop doing this!!
I have not seen this state in any other city.
The idea of taking the pics was that reaches the concerned authorities and they take some action. Now, just uploading the photos( around 50 of them ) would have been very boring. So, i decided to make a video with the photos, along with an inspirational song.
It is more than 2 months now but absolutely nothing has been done till now.
location: Mahadevapura, Bengaluru, Karnataka, India
sub_category_title: Clearance Of Garbage Dump Or Black Spot

title: Vehicle Horn noise issue
description:
My Apartment is facing the road side (Borewell Road, Whitefield) and vehicle frequency in this road is very high. I do not have issues with the vehicle noise made due to the travelling however nightmare is when drivers start awful honking, and it goes throughout the days & nights.

I have considered my options, like sound proofing my rooms but then, Soundproofing would cut out ventilation completely and if I keep any window open, vehicle horn sound would be severe. Think about the situation when you have your old parents, new born child or kids how they deal with such pathetic drivers’ honking attitude.

Honking is undoubtedly a perennial issue in any city, commuters keep honking because traffic rules are not enforced. Here I am also requesting others to come up with new/innovative ideas to deal with this worst situation. 

Keeping the concept of “NO HORN” Zone only works for few literate drivers, i thought of few other best solutions to this problem described as below. My options may be harsh for others but effective at the same time and this is not the time when we should react politely.

1- Instruct to heavy vehicle (tankers/truck/bus) manufacture to develop and fix such horns which must not have continuous sound when long press, horn sound must be intermittent no matter how hard driver presses. I don’t believe in providing training to the drivers. Responsible authority – Traffic police and civic authorities 

2- Stop selling such horns in outside/grey market-- if any driver installs any high decibel horns, penalize heavily; ask the reference of the shop who is selling such cacophony, approach and seal immediately. If driver doesn’t provide right contact, again penalize him for hiding the correct facts. Responsible authority – Traffic police and civic authorities

3- This option is real solution, every apartment must have two live cameras (one facing left, another facing right, if needed more), capture the video of drivers, which can automatically connect and send the data to traffic police, traffic police will send challan online/offline to concern vehicle owners. 
More complaints, more challans more revenue to Traffic police 

To mitigate this problem, create history and benchmark to other states traffic police must do the rightful job. Success of this problem will be measured by less honking. Responsible authority – Traffic police and civic authorities

I will attach video also to make people realize how hell this problem is. I suggest to concern department – If above provided solutions are not acceptable to you then you consider your options to solve this problem but do not close my compliant until proper solution provided. title: Road is worst in IT hub
description: Neeladri Road in Electronics City Phase 1 is in race for the worst road in any urban area.Electronics City is the official IT hub of India’s IT Capital Bangalore. We all will have a general perception that this place will be super developed as it houses to the premium IT companies like Infosys, Wipro, HP etc. It is true to a certain extent. The roads are clean and developed inside electronics city but as soon as the road leaves the company area and enters to the residential area, the scene completely changes. nYes I am talking here about Neeladri Main Road, Electronics City Phase 1. This is road is not far from the Indian IT boom story, yet thoroughly neglected. This area is having a real estate boom with lots of premium apartments, restaurants, super markets, villas etc. but the road is a torture to the nearby residents and to whoever uses it to travel in and out of Electronics City. 378 bus route more pollution route and next to Mumbai City. At a first look you won’t believe this road exists in Bangalore that too in back yard of India’s premium IT hub.nRecently ELCITA developed the road till Wipro but afterwards the road condition is pathetic. The road is full of potholes, potholes and bigger potholes.nProblem faced by people in this arean• Jam packed traffic in the evening and morning even with lesser vehicles compared to other area of Bangalore.n• You cannot drive straight due to the pot holes resulting the opposite flow of traffic.n• Each evening you can see standstill traffic with dead blocks.n• As the vehicles travelling slowly due to the bigger potholes, the vehicles coming from behind are trying to overtake and causing the opposite flow to stop. n• Each vehicle is trying to overtake as there is no median or road divider marks. n• This road is a hell for pedestrians. No place to walk on the road as there is no foot path.n• Road is full of dust and it is very difficult to go even in two/four wheelers forget about pedestrians.n• Dangerous for children to catch their school busses. nI am no urban expert and not sure who is responsible for the development of the road. I am not sure if it is responsibility of Central Govt, State Govt, BDA, BBMP, ELCITA, Area MP or Area MLA. But I am sure to repair this 1 KM stretch of road it will not take crores of money or years of planning. It is a small stretch of road and a proper road will benefit not only the residents of this area but also for those who travel thru this road to Electronics City.nPossible Solutionn• Pothole free proper road will solve 80% of the problems.n• Proper marking on the road as median is not possiblen• Foot path for pedestrians with drainsn• No Parking sign boards at proper places and crossings.nnThis Neeladri road being a newer area in Bangalore map, we expect this to be properly planned and good for living. If we cannot fix the problems of a new area then how age old problems of Bangalore can be solved. PLEASE HELP

address: Max showroom to SHELL Petrol Bunk

title: Bad condition of footpaths
description:
Hello sir/madam,

Bangalore is a metropolitan city where so many people from different parts of India come to live here and work here. We work in companies in Bangalore for the welfare of the city. Everyone knows that bangalore is a city of great MNCs. So it's obvious that people want to come here to work. 

People work in bangalore which will benefit both government and to their self. Bangalore is a costly city, the cost of living here is so much compared to other cities but still people come to this city to make their livelihood. 

It's your responsibility to provide at least basic facilities to the people who came here far away from their house. And the basic thing is good condition of roads.

As there are so many companies in bangalore, there will be so many people around the office at a distance of 2-3 km. They may prefer to come by bus or by foot. Even if they take a bmtc bus, they still wants to walk a certain distance to reach a bus stop. But here the footpaths are in such a bad condition that it looks like a mud path rather than a footpath. Even with a light drizzle, the footpath becomes so dirty that people have to walk on the bricks side to the footpath. Then what is the use of having footpath if people are walking on the bricks?

I am working in a company in ITPL, whitefield. There is a footpath between brigade bhuwalka icon to international tech park and from international tech park to the den hotel. The path in between itpl and den is so bad. It's in the worst condition. That path is full of mud and there are no cement bricks on it. And whenever rain happens it will become a mini pond. There will be hundreds of people walking in that path everyday. As bangalore state government, it's your responsibility to take care of these footpaths. 

If you are not able to make a full path of cement bricks, atleast make a row of those so that people can walk on it in a line. 

Please I request you to take care of these paths. Because of that mud, we are suffering so much. I again request you to please take care of these roads. I am not asking you to give us money or jewellery, nor we are asking to decrease our cost of living here. We are just asking you to give us proper roads because from morning till night, roads play a major role in our lives. Those are the main source which take us from one part to another part.

I really hope you take action on it as soon as possible because it is really needed.

title: Junk hill @ busy Junction
description:
It is said that Bannerghatta road is one of the fast-developing roads in all of Bangalore. But the photos attached to this complaint says otherwise. Don't believe it? The spot marked on the map and the photos explaining the scene is less than 10meters from the very famous Vega City mall. In spite of being one of the busiest roads with a lot of traffic. People usually swim through this heap of garbage to cross the Jedi Mara signal. I commute every day to my office using the same road having to see such blissful sight every day of my life. I have also seen people living nearby or just on the opposite side of the road throw food/plastic/wet/dry/degradable/non-degradable wastes and create such a beautiful mystery making it hard to classify the type of waste. But enough of all the jokes and sarcasm, let's get serious for a minute. I hope the below point will give a gist of the problem. 
1. I have witnessed a 2-wheeler rider fell and got badly hurt as he got out of balance when his vehicle moved over some wet waste. 
2. This is the welcome mat for people getting down from the BTMC buses. 
3. Because of this people are not able to use footpath and are compelled to get on the road to cross the street. And even when crossing one must take a deep breath so that your olfactory nodes don't get damaged. 
4. Since this occupies half of the road, commuters can use only the other half of the road. Many a time this causes serious traffic blockage. 
5. And since this is the heart of the rainy season all the dumped garbage gets clog the drainpipes and causes rainwater to overflow on the streets. 
Taking all these points into consideration, I request the concerned team/authority to take necessary actions and solve this issue. And I also ask to impose strict rules and heavy penality for irresponsible behaviors. Thanks in advance.

title: Access Road to Jal Vayu Towers Choked due to Parking on Both Sides of the Road
description:
There is a narrow road called Temple Road leading from the ESI hospital corner, behind Baiyappannahalli metro station, to Jal Vayu Towers (JVT) Apartments. Until just one year ago, the road used to be quiet and allowed easy vehicular movement. However, now the same road is always packed with vehicles parked on either side. Moreover, there are several taxis, buses, trucks, and a road roller parked there almost permanently. It is almost impossible for two 4-wheelers to cross each other, let alone a large fire engine to come through.

To add to this chaos, there is a commercial establishment called, “Maniranjan Diesel Sales and Services Limited” further up on the road that appears to have gone from a small quiet business to a large one, creating utter unruliness. Aside from several two-wheelers, there are large vehicles always double-parked in front of this establishment, either for loading or unloading, making it extremely difficult to use the road.

During development of this property Jal Vayu Towers has surrendered some of its land so that the road would be wide enough for a fire engine to come through in an emergency. However, now it seems that that was completely in vain and our fire safety is seriously jeopardized. 

We earnestly request the commissioner of Traffic Police Bangalore to investigate this matter. We recommend either making the entire street as non-parking zone with a limited number of assigned parking for the complex residents or introducing odd-even day parking ONLY on one side of the road. This is of utmost urgency for the safety of JVT residents.

title: Construction of the median
description:
The newly constructed median seems to have created the below inconvenience than in helping regulating traffic:
1. The area is mostly a residential area which needs pedestrians to be able to move around without obstacles. However, due to the height of the median, pedestrians cannot cross over to the other side of the road conveniently. A person now has to walk atleast 200-300 metres to reach a destination across the road from a particular point. It has to be noted that there are many senior citizens in this area who have knee issues and it is depressing to hear them say that they no longer visit neighbours on the other side of the road now because they cannot cross the road and the distance that they have to walk to reach the other side discourages them. Maybe for a young and abled body, this might not seem to be an issue. But for any old person and/ or physically disabled person, this is a huge challenge.
2. Residents are facing challenges to remove their cars from parking because of the traffic pile up which has increased after the construction of the median.
3. Traffic jams have increased after the construction of the median.
4. Noise pollution has increased after the construction of the median, especially closer to the milk booth/ sbi signal. This is leading to mental stress and hence physical distress. 
5. Ambulances seem to be stuck in traffic jam on the main road more now after the construction of the median.
6. The construction of the median might have hurt the business of the very small shops that are on the main road, and hence their livelihood.

I doubt if the width of the road allows for a median and even if it does, if the height of the median is scientific and appropriate. Request you to please relook into this matter and take feedback from the residents on the main road. 

Thank you.

The decay processes depletes dissolved oxygen in the water, often killing fish (or turtles). The plants also create a prime habitat for mosquitos,the classic vectors of disease, and a species of snail known to host a parasitic flatworm which causes schistosomiasis (snail fever).Please take appropriate measures before it destroys the aquatic ecosystem. We the residents of area near the lake request you to take prompt and quick action to resolve the matter  before it poses any threat to the residents near the lake!!!This lake is just not for beautification but life.

title: Change of meter type
description:
Our domestic connection all of a sudden changed to partial non domestic in Nov 2019. I enquired in the BWSSB Service station Kumarapark. The meter reader said there is a clinic in the first floor of the building. Apparently there was no running clinic in that building. We had put a board to apply for clinic license but the doctor withdrew and we removed the board. The supposed clinic was to be functional in the ground floor only after obtaining license from KPME. 

The meter reader verbally apologized and asked us to give an application and pay inspection charges to reverse the connection type. This person is now on long leave!

We gave a written application to BWSSB to reverse this meter type on 19 May 2020. We also paid inspection charge as per the department norms. Attached are the proofs. 

Three days after giving the application I even enquired with the concerned JE on how long it could take to resolve. I was advised that it will take 15d and in the bill of June it should be rectified. 

I enquired about the status yesterday 23 June and the concerned officer doesn't remember anything. Of course he has lot of work. I agree. But there must be some timeline in which there is an action.

So my question to BWSSB is: 
1.How can you authorise meter reader to change meter type without proper inspection of the non domestic water usage in the premises alongwith the resident or owner of the building?
If meter reader can change meter type  swiftly why doesn't reverse also happen swiftly?

2. Creating trouble for public is only your intention is it? The owner of the building - my father is physically handicapped. Do you expect him to run from pillar to post for your department folly? 
By creating trouble like this and expecting monetary benefits you delay the reversal process?

I am hoping to get swift resolution to this.

Thanks in advance.
Kusuma

title: Restoration of the only entry & exit road.
description:
This is a representation submitted by RAW (Rustambagh Association of Welfare) on behalf of its members and residents of Rustambagh to seek immediate resolution to the state of our road.

Rustambagh is a layout beside Manipal hospital (old Airport Road) with over 680 homes/families. Further to the work undertaken by BWSSB, our roads have been in a terrible condition. Despite complaining multiple times and regular follow ups, the single entry & exit road remains in a sad state, endangering pedestrians and motorists. Currently, the temporary mud layering of the road has begun to cave in.
With several senior citizens, frontline & emergency service workers like doctors and nurses residing in Rustambagh, it is quite impossible for them to even get to the hospital or for an ambulance to quickly come in to the layout, considering the bad state of our roads. The current condition has also caused minor 2-wheeler accidents and cars getting damaged while trying to traverse through the mess. 
We fear that if this state of the road continues, it will be a cause of threat to life, vehicles and emergency movement of our residents. Not to mention the significant inconvenience in day to day activities, involving movement of residents, entry/exit of water tankers and other essential delivery services particularly in these times of the Covid pandemic.
In this light, we seek your immediate intervention to fix the Rustambagh layout roads with proper layering and tarring, so that free movement is restored and the serious inconvenience to our residents is alleviated.
Kindly consider this on priority and do the needful at the earliest.

title: Suggestion for Clean Bangalore
description:
There are many vacant sites in our Layout and also in entire BBMP limits. The owners of this sites are not at all taking care or visit these sites. Many sites are turned into dump yards and senseless people are throwing plastic waste/all type of garbage on these sites and garbage dumps are formed on many sites. A lot of unwanted bushes and vegetation grown on these sites are not cleaned which gives scope for snakes and rodents to make their home. Some sites are being used for illegal activities at nights. Vacant Site owners are not bothered. Problem is only for those who have constructed homes in between and residing there.
I request you to forward my following suggestion to concerned higher authorities, which will resolve the vacant site menace and also create revenue for BBMP and make Bangalore clean.
Most of these sites are purchased for investment purpose and those owners are comfortably staying in nice homes in other parts of Bengaluru. If any person who is already possessing a home or having a site in his name or in the name of his spouse in BBMP limits, and if he has any vacant site in Bengaluru, then a time limit of say 1 or 2 years to be given for any construction activity on that vacant site. If it is not done, then as a penalty, BBMP or Govt can charge property tax at ten times the normal tax, and maintain such sites, neatly. Alternatively, by  amending the related laws, Govt can take over such sites by paying a compensation at the rate of purchase price plus indexation benefit. 
Land is a scarce commodity, and Govt can not allow anyone to hoard it. Land price is jacked up only due to hoarding. As many politicians are holding huge vacant land in BBMP limits,I am aware that my suggestion will not be looked into. But I believe that some sincere officials in BBMP apply their mind to above suggestion which is source of revenue to BBMP and make my Bengaluru neat and clean.

title: Absurd Noise Pollution caused by Cart Vendors
description:
I've lived in several areas of Bangalore, including Indiranagar, Whitefield, and Kammanahalli, and my particular area of RT Nagar is the most unnecessarily noise-polluted part of Bangalore I've encountered. The cause is cart-pushing vendors who use loudspeakers, and these are usually recordings that are on an endless loop. 

When I moved here two years ago, there were two or three vendors who used loudspeakers; currently, they number about 20. 

Two important points:
1) I am not opposed to cart vendors making a living in this or any other area; most of them simply use their natural voice to call out once every 10 or 20 meters. That's fine. Loudspeakers--particularly those with recordings on an endless loop--are unnecessary noise pollution that are a complete lack of consideration for the neighborhood. Many of us have to work online, conducting meetings and teaching classes, and banana salesmen using loudspeaker recordings should not have priority over the tasks of others who must work at home. 
2) My understanding is that these loudspeakers are already illegal in Bangalore, as I've read that any kind of public address system in this city must be at a volume that cannot be audible for more than 200 meters. I would like to see this law enforced, as this area is suffering from a great deal of unnecessary noise pollution that is impeding the productivity and peace of mind of those of us who work at home and those who simply want to enjoy a day of quietude.

In addition to the illegality and rudeness of these loudspeakers, I'll conclude by observing that many of these endless-loop recordings in my area are absolutely ABSURD in regard to the way they sound: It's as though the vendors deliberately created recordings that sound ridiculous, obnoxious, and agitating...and inexplicably believing such would attract a happy clientele.

title: Bull-Cow menace
description:
There are a large number of bulls, cows and calves that keep walking the streets of Teacher's colony, which is next to Venkatapura on one side and the Sarjapur Main Road on the other. 

In fact last year we helped with the birthing of a calf on our Street - 3rd Avenue out of love and compassion for the animals.  However, it seems to be posing a huge hazard to the citizens here.  Last Saturday, there were a bunch of bulls chasing a cow and to escape them I stepped on to the foot path and tripped and fell down and hurt myself very badly.  Luckily I did not fracture any bone in my body.  After this incident I also learnt from my friend who lives in the same area that she was caught in a similar situation and had broken her leg.  A couple of months ago I was returning home and at the Venkatapura junction a white bull and a black one were fighting on the road and came charging towards my vehicle.  Luckily some men in the shops came out and chased them away.  

All the streets are littered with dung, one night during a power cut and heavy rain, my maid accidentally stepped on the dung and fell down on the road. Imagine slipping and falling down on the road with dung all over you in a city like Bangalore.

These situations are really scary, it is playing with the lives of the citizens and their well being.  There are little kids playing on the streets, just imagine  a bunch of bulls chasing a cow at that time.  It will surely lead to a stampede and even death of the little ones. Before any major incident occurs this menace has to be brought under control and the animals be rounded off and not be let out on the streets once again.  

These are stray animals and belong to none.  Hence the authorities have to take up steps on a war footing to stop this menace.  Let us not wait for a tragic incident to hit the headlines and then wake up and take measures to do something about it.
location: Teacher's Colony, Hsr Layout 5Th Sector, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560034, India

title: Overflowing manhole
description:
The manhole on the intersection of the BTM 2nd stage 7th cross road and the Bannerghatta road has been overflowing for months now. There has been no action taken in this regard to resolve the issue. On contacting the BWSSB, I have always got the same response that they haven't got permission to dig up the road to resolve the issue. This sewage water is conveniently let into the drain and this finally ends up in Madiwala lake which could be detrimental to the marine life. The sewage water ends up covering most portions of the road and with the movement of vehicles splashing the stinking water all around, the stench is unbearable.
The sewage water from the overflowing manhole gets onto the road and there is an accumulation of silt which is a big accident hazard. Since this is the only main road linking 29th main Lake road to BG road, just imagine the bottleneck that would be created due to traffic when more than 50% of the road is unmotorable!
When there are heavy rains, the water gets into my residence and the stinking water covers almost 6-8 inches of the entire ground floor of the house. Every time there is heavy rain, it has become a real nightmare for us to clear out the water from the house and it has already caused enough property damage.

title: Movement of heavy vehicles & goods carriers during peak hours to be suspended

Dear Sir, 

This is to bring to the notice of traffic department to suspend the movement of heavy vehicles during office hours. Following a series of fatal accidents on city market flyover involving commercial vehicles, it is requested to restrict the movement of such vehicles during peak hours. 

To ease the movement of office / school goers and avoid congestion, the department has to take strict measures to avoid the movement of commercial vehicles during peak hours. Though the department has issued several notices to heavy vehicles to restrict the entry into the city during busy hours, the movement is not restricted. It has become a worst nightmare to commute on Nagarabhavi outer ring road, Nayandahalli juction and Mysore road market flyover during busy hours. 

Office goers are using the above said route to go to Central Bangalore areas like MG Road, Richmond Road etc; from Kengeri, RR Nagar, Nagarabhavi, Vijayanagar and other nearby areas.  During morning hours heavy vehicles and other loaded vehicles are allowed on the Sirsi Circle flyover causing congestion and traffic jams. I have witnessed 5 road accidents in one week; resulted in several deaths, including yesterday's accident on Sirsi Circle flyover. 

It has become extremely stressful to drive car / two wheeler during peak hours on the above said route. People are feeling more anxious while driving vehicles because of heavy traffic on Mysore Road. Moreover, overtaking from left and right on the flyover causing more stress to decent drivers. 

Request the concerned department to take appropriate action on the driver of heavy vehicles and goods carriers who are worsening the traffic during busy hours. A quick and favorable action of the above said route is highly appreciated. 

Thanks in advance. 

Regards,

With the onset of monsoons, it would be more difficult to manage. 10 minutes of rainfall would require hours to clean up. title: Dumping and Buring of Garbage / No response after multiple follow ups for months
description:
Hi Team, 

I Jafar Sadiq, resident of Shampura, Bengaluru - 560032, Karnataka. Want to take this opportunity to write to you on behalf of the residents of our locality to complaint about an ongoing issue which is not being resolved. 

I have been following up and sending emails for the past 2 months and not a single action has been taken. There still continues to be dumping of garbage, burning of the same, and that causing a great impact of the surrounding and health of elders. 

The smoke from the garbage being burnt entres the house and its awful. There is water clogging and that's increasing the mosquitoes and house flys and it's very scary as it can lead to serious health hazards especially to the kids and the senior citizens. 

I am reaching out to you with a lot of hope as my efforts of seeking help from BBMP have just gone down the drain. Never expected there are people who are so inconsiderate towards the wellbeing of the society and cleanliness of of city. 

This is really disappointing the way we have been treated for over the months. In fact the Health Inspector for the area has also been made of the situation but there isn't any action. 

I am sure whoever reading this is in much better position to understand our pain and daily suffering, and is also in a much better position to get things right for us and bring in a change.
